newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday with major institutions borrowing large amount of money to speculate on the active domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 10.38 percent from 7.36 percent on Monday.
Combined turnover rose to 7.37 million lots from 6.95 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The market rates, especially those of early-maturing contracts, were pushed up due to active trading in both Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets," said one trader.
The listing of a new A share firm, Tibet Shendi Co, also attracted liquidity from the repo market, traders said. Traders expect the rates to move around the current level on Wednesday.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday on institutional support after having fallen for weeks, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 124.21 yuan from 122.93 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market increased to 4.56 million lots from 3.14 million on Tuesday.
Traders believe the contracts will continue to rise in the next few days with sentiment improving after two days of rises.
